t.3.55.1: Bṛhadaśva said: When Bhaimī had chosen the Naiṣadha, the mighty guardians of the worlds, as they were departing, saw Dvāpara approaching together with Kali.
t.3.55.2: Then Śakra, the slayer of Bala and Vṛtra, having observed Kali with Dvāpara as his companion, said to him: "Kali, tell me, where will you go?"
t.3.55.3: Then Kali said to Śakra: "Having gone to Damayantī's svayaṃvara, I shall choose her, for my heart is set upon her."
t.3.55.4: Indra laughed and said to him: “That svayaṃvara is over. King Nala was chosen by her as her husband, right in our presence.”
t.3.55.5: Thus addressed by Śakra, Kali, filled with anger, took leave of all those gods and then spoke these words.
t.3.55.6: Since in the midst of the gods she chose a mortal as her husband, surely it would be just to inflict a heavy punishment upon her?
t.3.55.7: When this had been said by Kali, the heaven-dwellers replied to him: "With our full consent, Nala has been chosen by Damayantī."
t.3.55.8: And who would not take refuge with King Nala, endowed with every virtue, who knows all the laws completely and has duly observed his vows?
t.3.55.9: That king, a tiger among men, equal to the guardians of the world, in whom truthfulness, steadfastness, generosity, austerity, purity, self-restraint and tranquility are firmly established.
t.3.55.10: O Kali, whoever would wish to curse Nala, endowed with such virtues, that fool would curse himself and would slay himself by his own hand.
t.3.55.11: He would sink into a dire hell, bottomless, vast, and without a raft. Having spoken thus to Kali and Dvāpara, the gods went to heaven.
t.3.55.12: Then, when the gods had gone, Kali said to Dvāpara: "I cannot restrain my anger; I shall dwell in Nala, Dvāpara."
t.3.55.13: I shall make him fall from his kingdom; he shall not take his pleasure with Bhaimī. You too, entering into the dice, ought to lend me your aid.
